title: Fair runway allocator and latency SLA synchronizer
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Introduce a fairness-aware runway allocator for Dedicated fleets and synchronized latency-SLA signal propagation to improve throughput guarantees without destabilizing tail latency. Backwards compatible config defaults.
description: Motivation: Several tenants with short sustained spikes were observing either unfair runway grabs or transient SLA slippage when the fleet performed aggressive preemption. This PR introduces a Fair Runway Allocator (FRA) plus a Latency SLA Synchronizer (LSS). FRA slices the runway budget into time-windowed micro-allocations and assigns ephemeral fractional credits to tenants based on recent usage, committed capacity, and an adjustable fairness factor. LSS broadcasts smoothed p50/p95 latency targets to pool-level admission controllers so the allocator prefers allocations that preserve tail latency when pressure is high. Design summary: 1) runway ledger: lightweight in-memory ring per pool that records allocations as fixed-duration leases; 2) fractional credits: each tenant gets a soft budget that decays exponentially and refills on idle; 3) decision path: incoming provision request consults runway ledger + credit balance + LSS latency headroom; 4) graceful fallback: when credits are exhausted, requests are spilled to a probabilistic backoff with jitter and optional canary routing to cheaper model variants. Key safety goals: bounded allocation churn, no oscillation under moderate churn, preserve p99 tail for latency-sensitive tenants. Implementation notes: core allocator lives in pkg/autoscaler/runway_allocator.go and pkg/autoscaler/credit_bank.go; LSS signal wiring in pkg/telemetry/sla_sync.go and reconciler hook in controllers/pool_reconciler.go; added config knobs: runway.window_ms, runway.fairness_alpha, runway.max_fraction_per_tenant, sla_sync.window_ms. Backwards compatibility: default fairness_alpha is 0.2 which keeps behavior close to current conservative allocator; feature gated by config flag runway.enabled = true. Tests and validation: unit tests for credit decay and ledger semantics in tests/autoscaler/runway_allocator_test.go; integration harness simulates mixed workloads in benchmark-lab with convergent results. Performance: microbenchmarks on a 16-node Dedicated pool show steady-state increase in tenant fairness index (Jain's index) from 0.62 -> 0.84 for bursty tenants and median scheduling latency delta +3ms. Tail p99 latency increased < 1.5% for latency-critical tenants; overall token throughput unchanged. Rollout plan: staged rollout via canary on two clusters for 48h with auto-rollback if p99 tail increases by >5% or throughput drops >7%. Observability: new metrics runway.allocations, runway.credit_balance, runway.eviction_events, sla_sync.headroom_ms, and a small dashboard template under observability-pack/dashboards/runway-allocator.json. Migration and ops: migration is purely additive; operators can tune fairness_alpha and max_fraction_per_tenant per pool to trade fairness vs. throughput. Configuration example included in charts/dedicated/values.yaml. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration harness run - [x] Dashboard and alerts - [x] Docs: docs/ops/runway-allocator.md added - [x] Feature gating and default safe config - [x] Bumped telemetry ingestion schema version 2 -> 3 Changeset summary: commits below. Review notes: initial design reviewed in ENG-1489 thread; reviewers requested stronger safety nets around oscillation and an explicit max-eviction-per-window cap. Implemented a soft-rate limiter and eviction_budget in runway. Also addressed race around credit refills by switching to atomic update pattern and a single writer per tenant slot in the ledger. CI history: first CI run failed flake in e2e due to a flaky mock in tests/autoscaler/mock_clock.go; reworked tests to use deterministic virtual clock and re-ran CI. All checks green at merge. Merge: squash merged into main on 2026-02-24 by Priya Nair. Impact: improves fairness across tenants during bursty traffic while maintaining latency SLOs for critical workloads.

Introduces runway ledger, fractional credits, and latency SLA propagator to improve tenant fairness while preserving tail latency. Includes tests, docs, and dashboard.
